items.title: Codex builds your tasks and picks up where it left off
items.story: As a developer who sets workers = "codex", I get tasks built by a Codex worker through Forge's own SDK client, and fix rounds that continue the task's own conversation, so fixes come back faster without re-reading the repository and without the Claude Codex plugin.
acceptance_criteria: With workers = "codex", forge work runs one turn on a new named thread with full access; no app-server child remains after it exits, and a leftover one is stopped by the next forge work or forge doctor
Every approval request is declined and logged and never executes; forge work refuses if the declining handler can't be installed
Model settings come from the checkout's Codex settings; .codex/<kind>.config.toml may set only model, model_reasoning_effort and model_verbosity, and anything else refuses
Threads are named Build, Lite, Fix or Grill with the story/task or fix name and a title
The thread record is written before the first turn, and only one forge work runs per item at a time
Fix rounds resume the item's thread with the brief, new commits and working-tree diff; drift starts fresh with a reason; a changed approval refuses until re-approved
A turn left in progress is interrupted and awaited, and two turns never run for one item
Each turn writes one turn-log line with its status and token counts (null when omitted)
The first cold read runs on a read-only Grill thread; forge read --amended runs no model turn
With workers = "codex", forge doctor fails on a missing SDK environment or an untrusted project, and forge doctor --fix installs the pinned SDK
A stub contract test and a real smoke test against the pinned SDK both pass
Nothing outside history references codex-plugin-cc, and the guide documents uninstalling it
The plugin-removal task is built by a Codex worker, and its pull request shows one thread id across its build and a later round

items.title: The agent works as a forward deployed engineer; gstack removed
items.story: As an FDE without product training, the agent guides me through problem discovery, options and a payback-based choice, so that we build what measurably pays off.
acceptance_criteria: Discovery asks one question per turn with a Why-I-ask line and fills a problem card
New specs carry a complete success measure, checked after ship via a dated reminder in forge next
The payback rule gives the same recommendation for the same inputs
gstack and direnv are removed from Forge; client gstack files are untouched

items.title: Lean Forge v1: a simpler factory, rebuilt and switched
items.story: As an FDE or developer on Forge, I get one simple way to plan, build, review and ship on either Claude or Codex, installed as a pinned tool, with a plain-English board anyone can read, so we ship client value in minutes instead of fighting the factory.
acceptance_criteria: A story needs one doc, one cold read and one approval; every change ships as a PR through review (P0/P1 looped) and green CI
Workflow rules are enforced by forge commands and git hooks, with the PR check as backstop, identically on Claude and Codex
Clients install a pinned Forge tool; forge sync regenerates the adapter; forge migrate moves a vendored client in one PR
The board tells history and current state in plain English for non-technical readers
Switch checks pass: the FDE story end to end, a fresh client fix, and migrating a copied-in client; then the old tree is deleted

items.title: The coordinator can steer and question its Codex workers
The agent can merge a ready pull request when the owner allows it
One main chat approves every Forge repo's stories
Forge sheds dead and duplicated code before it grows again
Forge's Codex chats are easy to follow in the Codex app
Each Forge behaviour owns its own entry
A customer signs off a working prototype before any story exists
Design work (screens and flows) runs on Codex like everything else, but the owner wants UI and UX built by Opus 5.5 with impeccable, Emil and the app baseline, falling back to Codex Sol high

Salespeople can run the FDE route but trip on the engineering around it: they would have to merge pull requests, set up Node, Docker and test browsers by hand, see each small tweak wait for a full review, and hear Forge's words instead of the demo's

Forge can't tell a live production app from a prototype: without a sign-off record it applies prototype rules, it has no route to adopt a repo with history, and its pull-request check blocks the team's own branches
Gaps a plan never pins down come back as many review rounds, because the cold read runs once and nobody checks the amended plan

Forge covers building and sign-off records, but almost nothing the customer sees: no pre-meeting brief, no recap in their words, no realistic demo data, no demo script, no record of their reactions, and new projects are sent to a removed /office-hours step

Upgrading Forge in a client repo is blocked: the upgrade pull request can never pass Forge's check, close calls it clean with stale synced files, and the default branch refuses every command until the upgrade merges
The plan the owner approves is long and full of test lists, tasks and notes that only agents use

epics.title: Symphony Forge
epics.objective: Turn in-repo architecture and decisions into shipped applications through a deterministic software-factory workflow.
